name: Open Items
rows: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 · Ledgerwyn, Vellumrow, Charterfold and Quillpost · IT general controls workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · audit procedures · not an audit report · no opinion on internal control

Material weakness, proposed. The Controller administers Ledgerwyn, Vellumrow, Charterfold and Quillpost while she posts entries; the Ledgerwyn “admin” account is shared with Saltmarsh IT Services LLC; the Vellumrow vendor account stays enabled; the approval step is off and periods are never locked. 30 entries over $25,000, $8,045,083.44, had no second person (JE-01). Recommendation: give user administration to someone who posts nothing, retire the shared account, disable the vendor account, turn on the approval step and lock each period at close. The CPA decides the classification.

Significant deficiency, proposed (with ITGC-05). Mei Northcott can set up vendors, prepare and approve payments; she approved 4 payments to vendors she set up herself, $64,675.50 (SOD-01). Renata Salazar can edit the employee master and process payroll and entered her own unsigned raise, $10,000.00 a year (PAY-01). Recommendation: remove the approval right, approve every vendor setup, run and sign the master file change report each payroll.

Significant deficiency, proposed (with ITGC-02). Change VR-25-09 raised the AP Specialist’s approval limit from $10,000 to $25,000 on September 29, 2025 with no ticket, test or CFO approval (Q5). 3 later self-approved payments, $54,815.50, were above the old limit. Recommendation: every change, settings included, through a ticket, a test and the CFO’s approval.

Deficiency. 3 accounts of leavers were still active on July 31, 2026: Ezra Tamayo in Ledgerwyn; Renzo Valloton in Charterfold; Ezra Tamayo in Quillpost. Ezra Tamayo signed in to email on June 12, 2026, after the last day. No transaction followed. Cause: no leaver checklist (Q1). Recommendation: disable every account on the last day from one checklist.

Deficiency. Ledgerwyn passwords of six characters, no lockout and no multi-factor sign-in; 6 Quillpost accounts exempt from multi-factor sign-in, the AP Specialist’s among them (Q4); Charterfold passwords shorter than the policy. Recommendation: enforce the policy, and multi-factor sign-in for every account.

Deficiency. No user access review since 2023 (Q2), against the policy’s yearly review. The review would have found ITGC-01 to ITGC-03. Recommendation: each system owner reviews every user’s rights each year and the CFO signs it.

The control walkthroughs proposed SOD-01 and JE-01 as significant deficiencies and asked whether together they are a material weakness. These listings show the access behind them and the change that widened it. The CPA weighs both areas together.
Materiality is proposed at $340,000.00, 0.5% of revenue. The engagement partner sets it.

Management’s responses to the six comments, with owners and dates, have not been obtained. Significant deficiencies and material weaknesses go to the board in writing (AU-C 265); the CPA decides when.

These are draft workpapers and a draft findings memo for the engagement partner. They are not an audit report and give no opinion on internal control. Nothing has been changed in any system, signed, posted or sent.
